# AI contribution policy for declared

AI tools are welcome here, as long as a person stays responsible for the result. Every pull request must say whether and how they were used.

## What to write in your pull request

Add these lines to the pull request description (the template already has them):

```
AI-Disclosure: ai-assisted
Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5

- [x] I have reviewed every change in this PR and can explain it without AI help.
```

## Disclosure levels

| Level | Meaning | Accepted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `none` | No AI tools were used. | yes |
| `ai-assisted` | Written by a person; AI helped edit, refine, or fill in boilerplate. | yes |
| `ai-generated` | AI wrote substantial parts; a person prompted it, reviewed the result, and understands it. | yes |
| `autonomous` | AI produced it without meaningful human review. | no |

## Rules

- Every pull request declares exactly one level with `AI-Disclosure:`.
- If AI helped, name the tool and model with `Assisted-by: Tool:model` (the Linux kernel format). List several tools with commas.
- If AI helped, confirm you reviewed every change and can explain it without AI help. If you cannot, please do not submit it.
- The disclosure should match your commits. Many AI tools add `Co-authored-by` or `Assisted-by` trailers on their own; if yours did, disclose it.

## Commits

Marking commits is optional but appreciated:

```
git commit --trailer "Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5"
```

## How this is checked

An automated check reads the pull request description, commit messages and changed file names.
It does **not** try to detect AI-written code; it relies on honest disclosure.
If something is missing, a comment explains how to fix it and the check fails until the description is updated.

These are exempt from the check:

- bots and accounts: `dependabot[bot]`, `renovate[bot]`, `github-actions[bot]`
- repository roles: owner, member
- pull requests labelled `skip-ai-policy`
